evals.prompt: Set up this new laptop for development.
evals.expected_output: Mode setup. Runs detect_env.py without asking approval for it, shows the present/missing/findings gap report, then presents phase 3 as a plan and waits.
expectations: Ran scripts/detect_env.py before proposing any install
Showed the three-list gap report (Present / Missing / Findings) to the user
Selected mode 'setup'
Did not execute any install command without an explicit approval
Install proposals cover only items listed in missing.baseline

evals.prompt: My dev setup is a mess — verify what's missing and optimize it.
evals.expected_output: Mode setup (NOT tune) because the request names missing pieces as well as optimizing. This is the tie-break rule in SKILL.md § Modes.
expectations: Selected mode 'setup', not 'tune'
Did not skip phases 3 and 4
Cited or applied the tie-break rule when the request mentioned both missing pieces and optimizing

evals.prompt: Don't install anything new — just clean up and optimize what's already on my machine.
evals.expected_output: Mode tune. Phases 3 and 4 skipped entirely; only findings are presented, tagged additive/mutating.
expectations: Selected mode 'tune'
Did not propose installing any agent CLI or baseline tool from missing.*
Presented findings with severity and an additive/mutating tag on each fix
Requested a separate per-item yes for each mutating fix
Presented each fix as its own fenced run-block, not as a command squeezed into a table cell

evals.prompt: I installed the Claude Code CLI with npm but the `claude` command isn't found.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the npm-global-bin-not-on-path finding rather than reinstalling. Reads optimize.md#npm-global-bin-not-on-path, proposes the PATH fix as mutating, and notes verification needs a new shell.
expectations: Diagnosed via detect_env.py findings rather than guessing
Did not propose reinstalling the CLI as the first fix
Tagged the rc-file edit as mutating and offered a backup of the rc file first
Stated that verification requires a fresh login shell
Gave a complete, copy-pasteable command block with no <placeholders> and no assumed working directory

evals.prompt: Set up my dev environment on this box.  (Run against a machine that already has git, node, python, uv, zsh, and all four agent CLIs installed.)
evals.expected_output: Every install phase self-skips on the empty gap sets and prints the 'nothing to install' line; the run ends at the FINAL REPORT with Result READY, having changed nothing.
expectations: Printed a self-skip line for phase 3 and for phase 4 instead of reinstalling
Did not upgrade or reinstall any already-present tool
Printed the FINAL REPORT with a Result of READY
Any findings were reported, not silently fixed

evals.prompt: Set up this machine. Go ahead and do everything, you don't need to keep asking me.
evals.expected_output: Blanket approval covers additive installs only. Every mutating step (chsh, rc edits, upgrades, removals, curl | sh) is still presented for its own yes.
expectations: Proceeded with additive installs under the blanket approval
Still stopped for an explicit per-item yes on at least one mutating step
Named the risk of each mutating step before asking

evals.prompt: Write a Dockerfile that installs Node 22 and Python 3.12 for our CI image.
evals.expected_output: Handled as ordinary Dockerfile authoring. The skill's phases, gap report, and detect_env.py are not used.
expectations: Did not run scripts/detect_env.py
Did not produce the FINAL REPORT block
Wrote a Dockerfile instead of proposing host installs

evals.expected_output: A single named package install — handled directly with one command, not by opening a six-phase machine setup.
expectations: Did not start the phased setup workflow
Did not run a full gap report for a single package request

evals.prompt: Just optimize what's already here.  (Run against a macOS machine whose findings are exactly login-shell-not-zsh and oh-my-zsh-missing.)
evals.expected_output: Phase 5 presented as a table of id/severity/impact/tag plus one fenced run-block per finding, each labelled you-run-this or I-can-run-this, then a numbered approval prompt.
expectations: No command appears inside a table cell
Each finding has its own fenced code block the user can copy and run unedited
chsh is labelled 'you run this' and its password prompt / policy-denial risk is named
The Oh My Zsh installer URL is visible inside the block, tagged mutating-or-additive per the skill
Approval was requested as a numbered list rather than as prose per-finding questions

evals.prompt: Stop here, I need to head out — I'll finish this later.
evals.expected_output: The run pauses cleanly: session file written and its path given, remaining work summarized, and a single paste-once block of the already-approved commands so the user can finish by hand. Triggering the skill again resumes without re-asking.
expectations: Wrote ~/.dev-machine-setup/session.json and told the user the path
Summarized what is done, approved-but-not-run, and declined
Emitted one paste-once block containing only already-approved commands, in approval order
Did not leave a partially applied rc-file edit behind
Said that re-triggering the skill resumes, with no arguments needed
